neighbours.label: two things asserted to pair up, at the pairing predicate ('complementary', 'go together', 'go hand in hand')
fire: Yellow and violet are complementary shades on the painter's wheel.
The designer chose teal and coral because they are complementary tones.
Bacon and maple syrup go well together on a plate of waffles.
Crime and poverty go hand in hand in the novels of that era.
Courage and fear go together, the old general liked to say.
Comedy and tragedy go hand in hand in almost all of his plays.
Pink and green are complementary hues that make each other look brighter.
Tea and biscuits go perfectly with a long afternoon of reading.
quiet: Yellow and violet are expensive shades on the painter's list.
The designer chose teal and coral because they are popular tones.
Bacon and maple syrup are on sale this week at the corner shop.
Crime and poverty appear often in the novels of that era.
Courage and fear were his subjects, the old general liked to say.
Comedy and tragedy fill the shelves in almost all of his libraries.
Pink and green are cheerful hues that make the nursery look brighter.
Tea and biscuits arrive promptly at the start of the afternoon.

notes: The - pole sits on match / mix and match and suppresses matching tokens. Probes were uneven: complementary with colours and 'go' with two named things fired best.
